But I am also in an uncomfortable position with Jake Morrison. I told him two weeks. That was last tick. He called me directly, which is exactly what I told him to do. I have to be straight with him. I do not have a floor to put him on. I am a contractor, not a GM. But Jake has skills and relationships and if one of these job search conversations I started last tick opens into something real, I want him to know I have not forgotten him. chosen_actions.description: Accept Patricia Hawkins's 60-day contract extension at $4,500/month. Send a brief written confirmation acknowledging the terms: 60-day engagement, $4,500/month, deliverable is a written transition summary covering three-location operational model, EV certification status, and Q3/Q4 recommendations. I confirm commencement and propose an initial check-in call within five business days to align on the specific structure of the deliverable. I do not negotiate the rate — this is income I need and the work is within my existing scope. I will deliver something she can use.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Consulting income: +$4,500/month for 60 days ($9,000 total). Deliverable: written three-location transition summary with EV and Q3/Q4 sections.
chosen_actions.reasoning: The contract extension is the most critical action this tick. It extends my runway by two months at the moment savings are declining. My monthly burn against consulting income is negative — expenses are $9,969, income is $4,500, I am losing roughly $5,400 per month. Accepting this extension is not a strategy, it is survival. The deliverable is clearly scoped and I have the data to produce it. Patricia does not extend contracts on work that is not landing. This is confirmation the consulting relationship still has value. I accept immediately.

chosen_actions.description: Call Jake Morrison back directly — not email, a phone call — within the hour. Tell him the truth: I am a contractor working a 60-day extension with Patricia. I do not have authority to bring him back onto a floor I do not operate. What I can do is tell him what I know: the service lane at the surviving locations is the strongest part of the Regional Auto Group portfolio right now, and if he wants to pursue that avenue, Angela Wright is the person with authority over staffing decisions and I will make that introduction today. I also tell him that I have two conversations in progress with regional employers and if either of them leads to a role that has sales leadership or fleet account management components, I will call him before anyone else. I cannot promise him a job I do not have. I can promise him I am still paying attention.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Social capital, trust relationship. No financial exchange.
chosen_actions.reasoning: Jake trusted me enough to hold. I told him two weeks and he honored that. Loss aversion cuts both ways — I cannot afford to let this relationship corrode by going silent. He is a good salesperson with real relationships on the floor. If any of my outreach opens a door, Jake is the kind of person I want positioned near it. Being straight with him costs me nothing and preserves the trust. Giving him the Angela Wright introduction is concrete and actionable — something real, not just words.

chosen_actions.description: Advance the retraining transformation already in progress — specifically, this week I am preparing the written transition summary deliverable Patricia contracted for, and I am framing the work itself as the portfolio piece I will use in conversations with the two regional employers I contacted last tick. The deliverable is not just a contract obligation — it is the proof of concept for fleet service management and EV transition advisory as a service line. If either regional employer comes back with interest, I need to have something to show them that is current, specific, and demonstrates I understand where the market is going. The Patricia contract deliverable becomes that document.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Time investment: 15-20 hours producing the transition summary. Indirect benefit: portfolio material for parallel job search.
chosen_actions.reasoning: My skill relevance is 0.27 and falling. The in-progress retraining transformation I started at tick 10 is at 10% progress with a 10-month completion target. I cannot wait 10 months for the market to recognize a pivot I have not yet demonstrated. The fastest path to skill relevance improvement is producing tangible work product in the new competency area — which is exactly what Patricia's deliverable gives me an excuse to do. I am building the thing and using it to market myself simultaneously. This is how I close the skill-demand gap without waiting for a formal credential.

response.inner_monologue: The extension buys me two months. The job search buys me a future. I have to build both at the same time and not let either one become an excuse to stop working on the other.
